Invariably, this involves transforming plants into hostile, flesh-eating specimens and mutating beasts to rearrange organs, add joints to limbs, and cause them to secrete slime. In doing so, the faction hopes to gain the attention of alien entities they believe will descend and warp all worlds in their path.

The faction members are united in purpose but not in execution. Some pursue their own theories of mutation and transfiguration, experimenting on themselves as much as on other subjects. Some instructions communicated by the Starspeakers conflict with others, as though the alien entities they seek to communicate with weren't working in concert. These contradictions mean that the faction's work advances erratically, with rejected experiments as common as transformations deemed to be in concordance with the aliens' will.

**Dawnrise Canyon**  
Bringers of Cosmic Dawn members carry out most transmutations far from public scrutiny. The faction is based in the secluded Dawnrise Canyon, far below the clifftop where the Cosmic Oculus stands. The once-tranquil canyon is now a dangerous valley of frightening creatures, hostile plants, aggressive transmuters, and wandering aberrations drawn to the unnatural landscape. Time moves erratically in the region thanks to frequent use of time-altering magic to speed up or slow down specific mutations.

**Opposition to the Far Realm**  
While outsiders might not comprehend the distinction between the alien intelligences the Starspeakers commune with and the monsters of the Far Realm, Bringers of Cosmic Dawn members fear and reject the Far Realm as unknowable, indescribable, and inimical to life. The faction works to counter Far Realm incursions and expels any members who deal directly with that domain of incomprehensible horror.

# Leadership and Organization

The Bringers of the Cosmic Dawn lacks a rigid hierarchy, but its leaders maintain careful control over the information they receive from both members' experiments and alien intelligences.

**Member Roles**  
Certain members of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn have special roles in the faction.

**Starspeakers.** The five enigmatic Starspeakers command the entire faction. None answer to any name besides their title, and they rarely leave the Cosmic Oculus except to measure progress within Dawnrise Canyon. Four Starspeakers (Medium Aberrant Cultists) are human. The fifth and most senior Starspeaker appears to be an elderly human astronomer, but she is actually a magically disguised Aboleth who has eschewed the Far Realm.

**Worldwarpers.** Most faction members work at the Cosmic Oculus or Dawnrise Canyon, but others, called Worldwarpers, venture into civilized lands to engage in more far-flung experimentation. Worldwarpers seek out willing recipients to, as they put it, "gain blessings from beyond the stars."

Worldwarpers might offer to improve a banker's garden with voracious plants to deter thieves, provide an aberration to help guard a prison, or augment a diplomat's body to produce intoxicating pheromones. Like the work in Dawnrise Canyon, these puzzling changes ostensibly further a wider agenda, but Worldwarpers are rarely aware of the end goals; they merely put pieces in place as commanded and report back to the Starspeakers.

**Blots.** The Starspeakers secretly assign faction members to find and eradicate Far Realm sympathizers. These individuals, known within the faction as Blots, also venture into places where the Far Realm's stain bleeds into the world, seeking to quash the Far Realm's presence wherever they find it.

## Things Beyond the Stars

The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn receives messages from many alien intelligences, not all of which are aligned with one another. You can use the Alien Entities table to generate sample intelligences that are directing the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn.

**Alien Entities**

| 1d6 | Entity |
|---|---|
| 1 | Atropus, the World Born Dead, is a malevolent entity the size of a planetoid that drifts ever closer to the world. |
| 2 | Dendar, the Night Serpent, is a colossal beast that feeds on nightmares generated by its warped mind. |
| 3 | Tharizdun, the Chained God, is a dark spiral of roiling nothingness. It seeks freedom from its millennia-long imprisonment and the extinction of all life. |
| 4 | Xhalovix is an amalgamation of 9,999 mutated planets preparing to ascend to godhood once it has transformed its ten-thousandth world. |
| 5 | Trapped beneath a ruined city, Zargon the Returner seeks loyal worshippers to restore his mutation-steeped realm of slime and decadence. The dark sky reveals his malign will to those who know how to interpret it. |
| 6 | Ejected from the Negative Plane, a nameless evil entity drives mortals to despair by twisting reality into impossible forms. |

## Joining the Bringers

Transmuters might seek out the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn even if they don't wish to advance the faction's goals. Faction members are undeniable masters of Transmutation magic, and some daring characters might join long enough to learn their secrets. Although some transmuters escape the faction, far too many begin to believe the Starspeakers' ramblings and become devotees—or worse, they become unwilling subjects for experimental mutations when their disloyalty is uncovered.

## Cosmic Oculus

Once an abandoned observatory, the Cosmic Oculus became the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn's base when the faction discovered that the facility seems to magically amplify the messages of entities between the stars. In addition to the Starspeakers, faction astronomers also live in the Cosmic Oculus to record psychic signals from deep space and make nightly measurements of celestial bodies.

Most faction members never see the inside of the Cosmic Oculus. The ramshackle buildings clustered along the cliff face between the observatory and the canyon have expanded and mutated on their own, and members have used spells such as Stone Shape and Fabricate to haphazardly extend walls, enclose laboratories, and create passageways through the rock.

# Renown Rewards

Characters gain renown with the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn by engaging in aberrant transmutations or completing faction quests to recover rare ritual ingredients, samples of unusual flora and fauna, or astronomical measurements from distant locations. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

**Bringers of the Cosmic Dawn Renown**

| Renown Score | Reward |
|---|---|
| 3+ | You can freely enter Dawnrise Canyon, though you are afforded no specific protections from its dangers. |
| 5+ | The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn warns you when you travel near places with Far Realm influence or a significant number of Aberrations. |
| 10 | The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Scroll, Potion, or Wondrous Item category. |
| 15+ | 1d4 Cultists, convinced you embody a prophecy, become your loyal followers. You can order this retinue to assist you for one mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 20+ | You can buy Common and Uncommon Spell Scrolls that contain Transmutation spells from faction members. |
| 25+ | 1d4 Cultist Fanatics join your retinue of loyal followers. |
| 30+ | The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the faction teaches you its transmuting magic. You always have the Alter Self spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. |
| 40+ | You can buy Rare Spell Scrolls that contain Transmutation spells from faction members. |
| 50+ | Faction members openly share information with you. Additionally, the first time your Renown score reaches 50, you can undertake voluntary mutations to enhance your physiology. You have Advantage on saving throws made to avoid or end the Grappled and Poisoned conditions. |

# Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Characters

Most members of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn are transmutation-focused mages, but any characters with an interest in astronomy, aberrations, or warping life are welcome. New recruits aren't permitted to balk at the faction's creations or goals.

The most welcome recruits are Sorcerers (especially those with the Aberrant Sorcery subclass), Warlocks (especially those with the Great Old One Patron subclass), or Wizards (especially those with the Transmuter subclass). Characters with proficiency in Arcana, Medicine, or Nature or with Navigator's Tools are also valued as recruits, as are characters with the Cosmic Dawn Experiment, Guide, or Hermit background.

**Member Benefits**  
If you're a member of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn, you receive these benefits.

**Starwatcher Gear.** The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn provide you with Navigator's Tools and a blank notebook in which to record your astronomical observations.

**Trinket.** Roll on the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Trinkets table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn.

**Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Trinkets**

| 1d6 | Trinket |
|---|---|
| 1 | A razor-sharp, violet-tinted talon |
| 2 | An uneven spyglass lens that casts flickering pale-green light |
| 3 | A stone carved with stars in an unfamiliar constellation |
| 4 | Fragments of a prophecy about flumphs |
| 5 | A fern frond that twitches like a tentacle |
| 6 | A small box containing a worm that won't die |

# Using This Faction

The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn can easily serve as a villainous or amoral organization in your campaign. If the characters pursue villains to the Celestial Oculus, you can determine whether the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn fight the characters with the aid of powerful Transmutation magic and strange Aberrations, or if they turn out to be curious intellectuals duped by malign influences.

However, the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn need not be villains. The characters might need the faction's extensive knowledge of Transmutation magic to undo a shape-shifting curse or restore a transmuted ally to the proper form. Members' whispers about creatures from the depths of space might presage an incursion by conquering githyanki astride dragons or a fleet of mind flayers on spelljamming vessels.

# Special Facility

Members of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

## Transmutation Vat

*Level 5 Bastion Facility*

**Prerequisite:** Membership in the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn

**Space:** Cramped

**Hirelings:** 1

**Order:** Harvest

This laboratory features a vat or cauldron simmering with transformation potential.

**Harvest:** Fluid Transmutation. When you issue the Harvest order to this facility, you instruct your hireling to pour a substance into the vat and transform it into something else. You must expend a Common or Uncommon potion, which is destroyed in the vat. At the end of 7 days, the hireling produces your choice of a flask of Alchemist's Fire, a vial of Antitoxin, a vial of Basic Poison, or a Common or Uncommon potion of your choice.

**Enlarging the Facility.** You can enlarge your Transmutation Vat into a Roomy facility by spending 2,000 GP. When you issue the Harvest order to a Roomy Transmutation Vat, you can expend two Common or Uncommon potions. If you do, your hireling produces two substances of your choice instead of one; the options can be different.

name: Covenant of the Grave
description:
The Covenant of the Grave is a loose affiliation of necromancers and those interested in studying death and undeath through a disciplined, scientific lens. The covenant has no room for megalomaniacs who seek domination via hordes of undead minions.

These realists are aware that their studies, no matter how clinical, unnerve most people, so their members are unobtrusive and their laboratories hidden. The greatest covenant academy is the Pale Tower, a morbid, bone-white structure far from civilization.

# Goals and Activities

Covenant members are typically more interested in deepening their knowledge than their power. They freely share their research with each other via correspondence, personal visits, or clandestine lectures, but they rarely reveal discoveries to those outside the organization. Many worry that their research might be misused for sinister, nonacademic ends. Others simply don't expect anyone but like-minded scholars to comprehend their work.

Unlike necromancers who incite undead uprisings, the Covenant of the Grave usually works to stymie undead hordes and return less powerful undead to the safer confines of the laboratory or grave. Members consider undead rampages dreadfully unscientific, if not outright embarrassing. They're keenly aware of the harm that such villainous necromancy brings to the faction's reputation. Their opposition to necromantic wickedness sometimes puts the faction in conflict with powerful undead such as liches, death knights, or vampires.

# Leadership and Organization

Although an established hierarchy exists within the Covenant of the Grave, members are usually too engrossed in their own research to worry about rank.

## Necrodemics and Gravetenders

Any faction member who shares a significant scholarly truth about death, decay, or undeath with the faction might gain the title of Necrodemic. Some members hold expanded titles such as Arisen Necrodemic or Necrodemic Embalmist, awarded for sharing more complex knowledge.

The title of Gravetender is held by the three head administrators of the Pale Tower. Emeritus administrators keep this title after retirement, so four to six Gravetenders usually exist at a time. Gravetenders set the overall direction for the faction but are usually bookish and circumspect, so change within the faction is gradual.

## Joining the Covenant

Any spellcaster with an interest in Necromancy magic or macabre research is likely to hear about the Covenant of the Grave, but the faction doesn't actively recruit. The covenant expects aspirants to independently identify its members and present a well-reasoned proposal for membership. A member who receives a qualified aspirant usually confers with other members before either taking on the aspirant as a research assistant or sending them to study at the Pale Tower.

## Undead Members

Only a few members of the Covenant of the Grave are undead. Covenant members have little use for less powerful undead such as skeletons and zombies, and other undead are usually too consumed by their hungers to maintain the intellectual rigor the covenant expects. The Undead Members table details the few undead scholars in the covenant.

**Undead Members**

| Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Adlin Humbington | A bookish Ghost who haunts his surgical theater, Adlin is so tied to his experiments that he's unaware he's dead. |
| Kadra Faldrig | The Lawful Neutral Lich Kadra hides that she's undead so her highly regarded insights into lichdom seem inspired by intellect rather than a study of her own nature. |
| Melodin the Risen | A determined Revenant, Melodin is a Gravetender of the Pale Tower who seeks to avenge herself against her predecessor by proving herself the superior administrator. |

## The Pale Tower

The greatest concentration of covenant members resides in the Pale Tower. Rising from a noxious swamp, this bone-white structure is thousands of years old. The tower's small, dingy exterior belies its underground warren of classrooms, laboratories, and ossuaries.

In addition to being an academy and research institution, the Pale Tower is a repository of sinister necromantic magic that the covenant doesn't want misused. Rumors hold that malicious artifacts, lost Necromancy spells, and soul-staining magic items are locked away in vaults only the Gravetenders can access.

# Renown Rewards

Characters gain renown with the Covenant of the Grave by sharing scholarly insights into death or undeath or by completing quests for the Covenant. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Covenant of the Grave Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

**Covenant of the Grave Renown**

| Renown Score | Reward |
|---|---|
| 3+ | You receive free lodging at the Pale Tower and can access its extensive subterranean libraries. The covenant safely contains or destroys malevolent magic items you surrender to its care. |
| 5+ | You can purchase the costly Material components required for Necromancy spells you can cast from covenant members. |
| 10 | The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the covenant gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Rod or Wand category. |
| 15+ | Covenant members freely cast the Remove Curse spell on you and your allies. |
| 20+ | You earn the honorary title of Necrodemic. When you surrender a magic item to the covenant, the covenant gifts you a different magic item of an equal or lesser rarity from the same category as the surrendered item. |
| 25+ | You can arrange for a meeting with any of the faction's Gravetenders. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 30 | The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the faction shares necromantic secrets with you. You always have the Speak with Dead spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. |
| 40 | You earn the honorary title of Arisen Necrodemic. You can request the help of 1d4 Mages for one mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 50+ | If you or one of your allies dies and the body is brought to the Pale Tower, a covenant member casts a Resurrection spell, targeting the deceased. This reward is free the first time you use it. On subsequent occasions, you must provide any Material components normally consumed by the spell. |

# Covenant of the Grave Characters

Joining the Covenant of the Grave is advantageous to any character interested in the secrets of life and death. While intellectual rigor is important, knowledge of any death-adjacent subject is sufficient for aspiring members.

The most welcome aspirants are Clerics, Monks, and Wizards (especially those with the Necromancer subclass). Characters with proficiency in Arcana, Investigation, or Medicine; proficiency with Leatherworker's Tools; or the Covenant of the Grave Recruit, Sage, or Scribe background are also good fits.

## Member Benefits

If you're a member of the Covenant of the Grave, you receive these benefits.

**Grave Services.** The covenant respectfully performs final rites for your corpse whenever the inevitable comes to pass.

**Modest Lifestyle.** The covenant pays you a stipend that supports your Modest lifestyle (1 GP per day).

**Trinket.** Roll on the Covenant of the Grave Trinkets table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the covenant.

**Covenant of the Grave Trinkets**

| 1d6 | Trinket |
|---|---|
| 1 | A tin of grave dirt |
| 2 | A self-sterilizing trephine |
| 3 | A chapbook with illustrations of graveyards |
| 4 | A zombie's twitching toe |
| 5 | A small wreath of dried flowers in an old box |
| 6 | A mysterious organ in a jar of amber fluid |

# Using This Faction

Faction members might warn the characters of potential necromantic uprisings or escort the party through lands plagued with undead. Having access to graveyards and burial houses, the faction might also recover the corpse of someone the characters want to revive or question.

The covenant isn't likely to aid the characters for free. Members might request lost necromantic lore in exchange for their help or task the party with defeating a necromancer or undead creature who has rejected the covenant's academic overtures.

# Special Facility

Members of the Covenant of the Grave can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

## Morgue

*Level 5 Bastion Facility*

**Prerequisite:** Membership in the Covenant of the Grave

**Space:** Cramped

**Hirelings:** 1

**Order:** Research

A morgue is a location where corpses are stored and studied. You can store up to four Small or Medium corpses in the Morgue.

**Corpse Storage.** As long as this facility's hireling is present, each corpse stored in the Morgue is affected by the Gentle Repose spell. If the facility lacks a hireling or a corpse is removed, the facility's corpses or the removed corpse loses this protection until returned to a Morgue with a hireling.

**Research:** Cadaver Insights. When you issue the Research order to this facility, you instruct the facility's hireling to carefully inspect the corpses. This work takes 7 days. The next time you speak with the hireling, the hireling can share the cause of death of each corpse present and answer one question you have for each corpse as though the hireling had cast the Speak with Dead spell on it.

**Enlarging the Facility.** You can enlarge your Morgue to a Roomy facility by spending 2,000 GP. If you do so, the Morgue can store up to twelve Small or Medium corpses and up to one Large corpse.

name: Crucible Keepers
description:
The Crucible Keepers consists of daredevil evokers who venture into natural or magical disasters to study the phenomenal power at play. Some members use their Evocation magic to counter disasters and help others, while other members revel in nature's destructive forces and take inspiration from them to enhance their own devastating spellcraft.

# Goals and Activities

Crucible Keepers study Evocation magic to command energy and control powerful forces. They eschew solitary scholarship, preferring informal gatherings where they exchange ideas and try to impress their peers with spectacular displays of magical might.

Faction members might be thrill seekers, but they aren't fools. They plan their dangerous endeavors well in advance, spending days or weeks charting natural or magical phenomena before enjoying the rush of soaring through the eye of a hurricane or surfing a lava flow. They employ protective magic while engaging in these endeavors, and they're quick to chide fools who confront danger unprepared.

# Leadership and Organization

Those drawn to the Crucible Keepers aren't the sort who like following orders. Ranks within the Crucible Keepers are unofficial, fluid, and based on frequent competitive challenges between members, with losers acknowledging winners' higher rank. Challenges usually involve magical duels, elaborate races, or dangerous stunts.

## Joining the Crucible Keepers

The Crucible Keepers enthusiastically welcomes anyone who wants to try out for its ranks. Gaining membership is as simple as impressing any faction member with a clever display of Evocation magic, a wild physical stunt, or a dramatic parlor trick.

## Eljar Charscale

The current head of the Crucible Keepers is a dragonborn named Eljar Charscale (Medium Evoker Archmage; see chapter 6). Originally a human, Eljar was executed by cruel generals when he refused to use his magic in an unpopular war. After his allies reincarnated him, Eljar fled in his new dragonborn body. He took the name Charscale on joining the Crucible Keepers.

Eljar loves the thrill of Evocation magic and is undefeated in duels of spellcraft. In addition to his magical talent, Eljar is respected for listening to everyone and offering sensible guidance. He began leading the Crucible Keepers only a few months ago after the former leader died in a forest fire.

Eljar has a strong antiwar stance that he disseminates throughout the organization. He has forbidden members of the Crucible Keepers from serving as military battle mages. Some evokers believe this stance restricts their career paths, but most understand the reasoning behind Eljar's policy.

## Disaster Chasers

Crucible Keepers predict and study natural and magical disasters, both to warn those who will be affected and to explore nature's incredible power. You can roll on or choose a result from the Pending Disasters table to generate a sample disaster Crucible Keepers plan to address.

**Pending Disasters**

| 1d4 | Disaster |
|---|---|
| 1 | An undersea volcano near a busy bay is showing signs of an imminent eruption. Crucible Keepers who can operate underwater rush to study it and warn those nearby of its dangers. |
| 2 | Oracles predict a terrible earthquake will devastate a metropolis in the next few weeks. Crucible Keepers race to construct magical pylons to absorb its earth-rending energy. |
| 3 | A gate to the Elemental Plane of Fire is expected to appear in remote farmland. Crucible Keepers hope to stabilize and eventually close the gate—but before closing it, they want to venture through it to study planar conflagrations. |
| 4 | An ancient white dragon that planned to bury a peaceful valley beneath an avalanche has been slain. Crucible Keepers study the weakened snowpack so they can redirect the avalanche away from the nearby villages. |

## Caldera Arcadium

Although members believe that nature is the best classroom, the Crucible Keepers maintains a learning institution focused on Evocation magic. The Caldera Arcadium is a large stone building hanging over the rim of an active volcano, suspended by enormous metal chains and struts.

The temperature inside the building ranges from unpleasantly warm to blisteringly hot, but eager students fill its three classrooms every day. The building also holds magical forges for the study and creation of magic items. A stone bridge from the Arcadium's roof leads to dormitories, academic offices, and a cafeteria, all hanging off the volcano's edge.

The Caldera Arcadium's headmaster is a scholarly Efreeti named Nadia Flameheart, who taught magic in the City of Brass for a millennium before joining the Crucible Keepers. The only wishes she entertains are those for better grades, and her only responses are tips for studying.

Fire-blackened Stone Golems called the Scorchborn provide security for the Arcadium, a duty that mostly involves defusing fights between hotheaded students. The Scorchborn are also instrumental to the wards that protect the school from volcanic eruptions, but not even Nadia Flameheart understands how. Since all Scorchborn are identical, no one is sure how many there are. No danger has yet presented a sufficient threat to marshal them all in one place.

Arcadium students frequently engage in death-defying stunts they call "field trips." The most common stunt is a leap from an Arcadium balcony during an eruption, trusting an ordinary rope to prevent a fall into lava. Another popular field trip involves launching homemade hang gliders from the volcano's edge.

# Renown Rewards

Characters gain renown with the Crucible Keepers by surviving natural disasters or by completing Crucible Keeper missions. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Crucible Keepers Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

**Crucible Keepers Renown**

| Renown Score | Reward |
|---|---|
| 3+ | The Crucible Keepers sends you advance notice of natural disasters in your area. |
| 5+ | The Crucible Keepers permits you and your companions to stay at the Caldera Arcadium. |
| 10 | The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Crucible Keepers gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Wand or Weapon category. |
| 15+ | You can buy Common and Uncommon Spell Scrolls that contain Evocation spells while at the Caldera Arcadium. |
| 20+ | A reckless Mage Apprentice becomes your loyal fan. You can order this apprentice to assist you for one mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 25+ | Eljar Charscale or Nadia Flameheart meets with you at your request. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 30 | The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the Crucible Keepers teaches you magic to guard you from the elements. You always have the Daylight spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. |
| 40+ | Faction members openly share information with you. You can buy Rare Spell Scrolls that contain Evocation spells while at the Caldera Arcadium. |
| 50+ | You can call for an Efreeti to aid you with a single task; the DM determines whether the efreeti can grant a Wish. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |

# Crucible Keepers Characters

The Crucible Keepers welcomes anyone willing to study destruction up close, which brings a high proportion of daredevils and thrill seekers into its ranks. Characters who are Barbarians, Druids, Sorcerers, or Wizards (especially those with the Evoker subclass) are likely to be sought after as members, as are those with proficiency in Intimidation, Nature, or Survival or with the Crucible Storm Chaser or Noble background.

## Member Benefits

If you're a member of the Crucible Keepers, you receive these benefits.

**Poor Lifestyle.** The Crucible Keepers pays you a stipend that supports a Poor lifestyle (2 SP per day).

**Trinket.** Roll on the Crucible Keepers Trinkets table to determine what trinket you have from your time in the Crucible Keepers.

**Crucible Keepers Trinket**

| 1d6 | Trinket |
|---|---|
| 1 | A piece of metal pierced by a tornado-driven twig |
| 2 | A tattered, salt-stained doll |
| 3 | A chunk of volcanic glass |
| 4 | Broken wind chimes |
| 5 | A seashell blackened by a great fire |
| 6 | Bark seared with lightning-shaped lines |

# Using This Faction

Crucible Keepers are often harbingers of catastrophe. If they appear in large numbers, it's usually because they anticipate an imminent disaster. A Crucible Keeper traveling through a dangerous area might hire the party to escort them, but it would be wise to ask what awaits at the journey's end.

However, Crucible Keepers are evokers, not diviners, so their guesses are sometimes wrong. As the DM, you can decide whether that means the disaster doesn't happen, is earlier or later by days, or is some other event entirely.

Crucible Keepers also study the aftermath of disasters, both natural and magical. Their presence might be a detriment or a blessing for recovery efforts. Unscrupulous members revel in disasters' aftermath and might seek to profit from them, while selfless members work to ease suffering.

# Special Facility

Members of the Crucible Keepers can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

## Geothermal Vent

*Level 5 Bastion Facility*

**Prerequisite:** Membership in the Crucible Keepers

**Space:** Roomy

**Hirelings:** 1

**Order:** Empower

A geothermal vent draws heat from deep below the surface to provide energy and power simple machines.

**Empower: Withstand Heat.** When you issue the Empower order to this facility, for the next 7 days, the facility's hireling teaches a series of meditative techniques that allow a character to mitigate the injuries they suffer from flames. Any character who trains here for at least 8 hours on each of those days gains the following benefit at the end of the training period:

**Heat Tolerant.** When you take Fire damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce this damage by 1d4 plus your level. This benefit lasts for 7 days.

**Hot Water.** Your basic facilities benefit from a constant source of adjustable heat. For example, a dining room has a warming table to keep food hot, a kitchen has multiple ovens with varying heat, and a bedroom has a basin that warms water for washing.

name: Cult of the Dragon
description:
The Cult of the Dragon is a centuries-old cabal of evil mages, doomsayers, and dragon worshipers. Its members believe in apocalyptic prophecies that center on dragons as the world's inevitable destroyers (or, rarely, its saviors). To hasten the end times, cultists enact elaborate rituals to empower or summon evil dragons.

**Goals and Activities**  
The plots of the Cult of the Dragon are secret, but its existence isn't. Most folk in Faerûn have heard of the cult but know only that its members revere evil dragons. The cult recruits new members in major cities, where many cultists engage in legitimate business or are assigned to ordinary academic research. Only a few serve as thieves, assassins, and spies.

At its outset, the Cult of the Dragon primarily concerned itself with the creation and worship of dracoliches - powerful undead dragons the cult believes will inevitably rule Faerûn - through rituals detailed in the Tome of the Dragon. More recently, however, the cult has splintered, with many within the cult committing themselves to Tiamat, the evil Queen of Dragons. This splinter group elevates Tiamat above other divinities and looks forward to the Dragon Queen's return, believing that she—not dracoliches—will destroy civilization, usher in a glorious reign of dragons, and reward those who helped bring about draconic rule.

Dragon-themed symbolism and iconography pervade the cult's regalia: a cape or cloak cut to resemble dragon wings, plus clothing, jewelry, and draconic accessories reflecting the wearer's favorite type of dragon. Masks—especially masks of dragons—are common at cult gatherings, and many cultists craft their own masks.

Cultists avoid wearing this regalia in public, but anyone who knows what to look for can often pick an incognito dragon cultist out of a crowd. The most recognizable tell is the sign of Tiamat, a gesture cultists who revere the Dragon Queen use to greet one another: right hand extended, palm forward, with five fingers spread in imitation of Tiamat's five heads.

**Leadership and Organization**  
The cult has a simple hierarchical structure, consisting of initiates on the bottom, four ranks for cultists, and one highest rank for the Wearers of Purple—the leaders and cult masters of particular locales. The cult is ruled by secretive Wearers of Purple called wyrmspeakers—a term of respect given to those whose bond with dragons is supernaturally strong.

Rank in the cult is based on merit and fanaticism. As raw recruits, initiates have no rank and follow the orders of their superiors. Only initiates that prove their worth can advance. A Wearer of Purple can promote an initiate along the track of dragonclaw (first rank), dragonwing (second rank), dragonfang (third rank), and dragonsoul (fourth rank).

Cult operation groups vary in size, from a few low-ranking cultists operating on their own to hundreds of cultists of various ranks under the control of multiple Wearers of Purple, depending on their assigned tasks.

**Cells**  
The Cult of the Dragon consists of countless cells spread across Faerûn. Each cell is led by one or more Wearers of Purple who report to the cult's wyrmspeakers, typically via magical correspondence. Cells have their own agendas but must conform with the wyrmspeakers' doctrine or else face expulsion from the order.

Low-ranking cultists have little reason and few opportunities to interact with cultists outside their own cell.

**Recruitment**  
The Cult of the Dragon is always seeking to expand its ranks. New recruits are encouraged to bring trusted family members and friends for conversion. The next most common form of recruitment is tried-and-true abduction combined with cult indoctrination. Cultists also sometimes recruit undead, fey, or other monsters.

Cult leaders aren't opposed to hiring mercenaries for specific jobs or when ranks are thin. The cult casts a wide net with vaguely worded fliers on job boards or shadowy brokers posted in dark tavern corners; higher-ranking cultists then cherry-pick the most promising (that is, manipulable) prospects. In this way, countless soldiers of fortune, run-of-the-mill toughs, and even seasoned adventurers have unwittingly undertaken missions for the cult. Some complete their job none the wiser of their involvement in the cult's schemes. Others discover the ruse in time to flee. An unsavory few catch on to the true nature of their work and use the opportunity to seek admission to the cult.

**Wearers of Purple**  
The Wearers of Purple stand at the top of the cult's hierarchy, and their word is law for the cultists in the cities, strongholds, and lairs they command. They are the only members of the cult to wear purple, and most are proud enough to flaunt the color. The Wearers of Purple have an affinity for talking to and negotiating with dragons—the gift of wyrmspeaking. Dozens of Wearers of Purple are spread throughout the Cult of the Dragon, and all can marshal the cult's resources at will.

Only the cult's inner circle can promote a dragonsoul to a Wearer of Purple, granting that character a base of operations and funds. Most new Wearers of Purple have already developed a working relationship with a dragon or dracolich as part of their power and authority. Those who don't cultivate this relationship are sometimes demoted. Several priests of Tiamat have recently been made Wearers of Purple and are establishing temples for her open worship in Faerûn.

**Wyrmspeakers**. Five Wearers of Purple conduct the cult's farthest-reaching plans. The members of this inner circle each wear a different colored dragon mask that hides their true identities. They call themselves wyrmspeakers, and members of the cult fear their power over dragons. Each wyrmspeaker has an affinity for a particular color of chromatic dragon. They treat with dragons of those colors to recruit more dragons to the cause, and plan cult missions that advance the cult's plots.

**Leaving the Cult**  
Once initiated, a cultist belongs to the cult for life. Those who escape the cult spend the rest of their days fearful of every shadow and stranger, for the cult doesn't take kindly to deserters. In exceptionally rare cases, a cult member might be excommunicated yet allowed to live. The price of this mercy is never cheap; exiled cultists must usually give up all their memories to mind-obliterating magic or commit some unspeakable act the cult can later use as blackmail if needed.

# Renown Rewards

Characters gain renown with the Cult of the Dragon by working with dragons or by completing quests for the cult. As their Renown Score increases, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Cult of the Dragon Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, your DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

**Cult of the Dragon Renown**

| Renown Score | Reward |
|---|---|
| 3+ | The Cult of the Dragon provides you a Poor lifestyle for free at its hideouts. |
| 5+ | You can hire Cult of the Dragon hirelings for half the usual cost. |
| 10 | You receive the honorary rank of dragonclaw. The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the cult rewards you with one random Uncommon magic item. |
| 15+ | You receive the honorary rank of dragonwing. You can assign a squad of up to six Cultists to perform any task that doesn't directly conflict with the cult's doctrine. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 25+ | You receive the honorary rank of dragonfang. You can request the aid of one Cultist Fanatic for a mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 30 | The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the cult rewards you with one random Rare magic item. |
| 40+ | You receive the honorary rank of dragonsoul. You can call in a favor to make a specific Humanoid creature "disappear" for 1d10 days. You must know the name of the target creature, but you don't need to know their location. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 50+ | You receive the honorary rank of Wearer of Purple. All cultists obey your instruction and openly provide you information. In addition, you can request an audience with the cult's inner circle. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again. |

# Cult of the Dragon Characters

The Cult of the Dragon attracts members from all walks of life; soldiers, spellcasters, and scoundrels all have skills valuable to the cult.

Any character might associate with the Cult of the Dragon, even those who aren't evil. Desperate times can push good-natured people to beseech the cult for a favor. Cultists often blackmail innocent people—including cultists' own family members—into doing work for the cult. A character could be aiding the cult unwittingly (even if you, the player, know the truth).

**Member Benefits**  
If you're a member of the Cult of the Dragon, you receive the following benefits.

**Tithing.** You are expected to donate 100 GP or 10% of your earnings per month, whichever is less, to the leader of your cult's cell.

**Trinket.** Roll on the Cult of the Dragon Trinkets table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Cult of the Dragon.

**Vestments.** As part of your initiation, you receive a set of Robes and a sinister dragon mask. You choose the color of these vestments: black, blue, green, red, or white.

**Cult of the Dragon Trinkets**

| 1d6 | Trinket |
|---|---|
| 1 | A dragon claw pendant on a leather cord |
| 2 | Ashes of a dracolich in a small brass canister |
| 3 | A map of an unknown dragon's lair |
| 4 | A black pearl etched with a Draconic rune |
| 5 | A drop of dragon's blood preserved in amber |
| 6 | A scrap of purple silk |

# Marked by the Dragon

The Cult of the Dragon conducts sacrificial rituals to advance its esoteric goals. But not all the cult's sacrificial victims perish in the ordeal. A rare few emerge from the ritual not just alive, but changed. Such survivors are said to be "marked by the dragon." Some call these individuals dragonscarred. Different cells treat dragonscarred differently. Some view them as monstrous and exile them from the cult's territory. Others treat dragonscarred well, elevating them to higher stations in the cult.

If your character has undergone a sacrificial ritual and yet survived, you can roll on the Dragonscarred Blessings table to randomly determine the physical feature your character bears from the ordeal. These features are superficial and serve no practical function.

**Dragonscarred Blessings**

| 1d8 | Physical Feature |
|---|---|
| 1 | You bear a facial scar in the shape of a dragon. |
| 2 | You have vestigial dragon horns, vestigial wings, or a vestigial tail. |
| 3 | Your eyes have slitted pupils and vividly colored irises. |
| 4 | Parts of your skin are covered in patches of reptilian scales. |
| 5 | Your blood is icy cold. |
| 6 | A flame crackles inside your chest, and you exhale bits of ash with every breath. |
| 7 | You crave and can digest foods your species would normally find inedible, such as whole eggs, raw poultry, dirt, or bones. |
| 8 | Your hair stands on end and crackles with static electricity. |

# Special Facility

Members of the Cult of the Dragon can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

**Cult of the Dragon Archive**  
*Level 13 Bastion Facility*

**Prerequisite:** Membership in the Cult of the Dragon

**Space:** Roomy

**Hirelings:** 1

**Order:** Research

A Cult of the Dragon Archive contains extensive records on specific topics, including dragons.

**Research:** Helpful Lore. When you issue the Research order to this facility, you commission the facility's hireling to search the archive for lore. The work takes 7 days. The hireling gains knowledge as if they had cast the Legend Lore spell, then shares this knowledge with you the next time you speak with them.

**Reference Books.** Your Cult of the Dragon Archive contains a collection of draconic lore. You have Advantage on Intelligence (Nature or Religion) checks you make in your Bastion when you take the Study action to recall lore about Dragons, Tiamat, or the Cult of the Dragon.

Enlarging the Facility. You can enlarge your Cult of the Dragon Archive to a Vast facility by spending 2,000 GP. If you do so, you gain two reference books chosen from those listed in the Archive entry in chapter 8 of the Dungeon Master's Guide.

name: Cults of Innsmouth
description:
Four cults operate in Innsmouth, each with its own vile ends. While these groups are ruinously evil, characters might temporarily ally with one or more to oppose another foe or to escape the domain.

# Cults and Cultists

The following groups vie for power on and under Innsmouth. Following each cult's name are the ritual words cult members use in their blasphemous practices, along with other details.

## Cult of the Chthonic Night

*Hail, Hail, Cthulhu Awaits*

**Worships:** Cthulhu  
**Leader:** King-Priest Eeyog-Yah  
**Goal:** Free Cthulhu from imprisonment  
**Lair:** The village of Innsmouth and the Vaults

Initiates of the Cult of the Chthonic Night open their minds to the whispers of Great Cthulhu and seek to free the imprisoned terror from the Domains of Dread. Predominantly composed of Aberrant Cultists and Kuo-toa that dwell amid waterlogged ruins deep below the Graven Peak, the cult interprets visions from Cthulhu as omens, calls for sacrifice, and signs of their god's coming.

King-Priest Eeyog-Yah, an ageless and desiccated Kuo-toa Archpriest, leads the cult. Eeyog-Yah occupies a state of perpetual somnambulism and narrates its visions. The priest's attendants decipher their leader's rambling as directives from their god.

Those who join the cult and participate in its induction rituals hear the voice of Cthulhu more clearly than others do.

## Cult of the Drowning Wave

*Make Clean for the Aeon Wave*

Worships: **Olhydra**  
Leader: **Draa Shoom**  
Goal: **Sink Innsmouth below the waves**  
Lair: **Eyes of Olhydra**

Those who await the Drowning Wave seek to make Innsmouth and all its inhabitants part of Olhydra's realm on the Elemental Plane of Water. Olhydra, the Prince of Evil Water, then could use the might of Cthulhu and the mass sacrifice of the island to dominate the Elemental Planes and flood the Material Plane.

Draa Shoom, the cult's Aboleth leader, believes Olhydra will return the cult to a place of dominance over countless worlds in return for its sacrifice. To effect this, Draa Shoom coaxes Elemental Cultists and shipwrecked individuals to the Eyes of Olhydra. There, amid boggy ruins and the lairs of murky elemental creatures, rises the Fathomless Gate. This ancient stone arch, thought to connect to the Elemental Plane of Water, is covered by bars of starmetal, which prevent passage by solid creatures. The cult seeks the proper rituals to open the gate, allowing Olhydra's scouring waters to flood the domain.

Those who participate in the cult's induction rituals are infused with a draught of Olhydra's sapient form.

## Cult of the Heavenly Doom

*Empty Yourself to Gorge on the Stars*

**Worships:** Zhudun  
**Leader:** Celesta Grayl  
**Goal:** Open gateways to join Zhudun  
**Lair:** Blind Observatory and the Map of the Eclipse

Among the broken heights of the domain, the obsessed astronomers of the Cult of the Heavenly Doom seek signs in the heavens and omens from Zhudun, the Corpse Star, an Elder Evil that wanders space and knows the secrets of extinction. These cultists hope to climb into the heavens and join Zhudun.

The cult's leader, Celesta Grayl, has sought Zhudun for centuries. While documenting her observations, Grayl discovered a path to immortality and became a Vampire Umbral Lord. Death Cultists, along with desperate and deluded souls, have flocked to the ancient stargazer, forming the cult around Grayl and her discoveries despite their leader's protestations and predations. The vampire suffers the cultists only so long as they help her decipher secrets from ruins around the island and retrieve knowledge from the grip of other cults. She believes their discoveries will help her reveal when the stars are right to join Zhudun in the dark places between the stars.

Those who join the cult and participate in its induction rituals release a portion of their life to the stars.

## Cult of the Scaly Abyss

*The Prince Awaits—Become the Way*

**Worships:** Dagon  
**Leader:** Xr'gh  
**Goal:** Summon Dagon  
**Lair:** Dagon's Claws

The followers of Dagon, Demon Prince of the Darkened Depths, lurk among and beneath the waves of Innsmouth. Ancient even among inhabitants of the Abyss, Dagon seeks to drag demon lords and their Abyssal realms into its demesne of Shadowsea. Once sated on the flesh of its foes, Dagon aspires to unleash its might across the multiverse in a sanity-shattering wave.

Xr'gh, a Sahuagin Baron fanatically devoted to Dagon, seeks to turn all who dwell beneath the waves to the demon lord's worship. Xr'gh seeks enough sacrifices to turn the sea red with blood, an offering great enough to attract Dagon's notice and draw the demon lord to Innsmouth. The cult leader expects Dagon then to feed on Cthulhu and begin its conquest of the Abyss. Ravenous Sahuagin follow Xr'gh, as do Fiend Cultists and murderers desirous of the eerie gold treasures the sahuagin offer from their submerged vaults. The Cult of the Scaly Abyss hunts the domain's ruined villages, abducting anyone who seeks shelter amid the wreckage. Those they find, they drag through secret paths beneath the waves to their ritual site under the island called Dagon's Claw.

Those who join the cult and participate in its induction rituals develop shark-like organs.

# Cult Rites

The cults of Innsmouth seek initiates to aid in their unfathomable works. Those who prove themselves reliable devotees gain access to the transformative power of strange gods.

## Cult Renown

The cults of Innsmouth reward those who honor their obscene patrons. Use the guidance in the Dungeon Master's Guide to track characters' individual standing within Innsmouth's cults. Characters can gain renown with a cult by performing deeds such as those in the Innsmouth Cults Renown table.

**Innsmouth Cults Renown**

| Deed | Renown Gained |
|---|---|
| Slaying an enemy cultist | +1 |
| Despoiling an enemy ritual site | +1 |
| Participating in a cult ritual | +1 |
| Ritual sacrifice of an enemy or magic item | +2 |
| Retrieving alien devices | +2 |
| Disrupting an enemy ritual | +3 |
| Slaying the leader of an enemy cult | +5 |

*Renown for this deed can be gained only once per week.

## Cult Dark Gifts

Characters who have a Renown Score of 10+ with an Innsmouth cult are honored as the chosen of the cult's patron. They are urged to take part in a ritual that inducts them into the cult and bestows on them a supernatural boon. A character who participates in such a ritual gains the Dark Gift noted on the Innsmouth Cults Dark Gifts table.

**Innsmouth Cults Dark Gifts**

| Cult | Dark Gift |
|---|---|
| Cult of Chthonic Night | Gathered Whispers |
| Cult of the Drowning Wave | Symbiotic Being |
| Cult of the Heavenly Doom | Touch of Death |
| Cult of the Scaly Abyss | Aberrant Anatomy |

These Dark Gifts include magical transformations associated with the cult's patron and its members. This magic can make it easier to navigate parts of the domain and bypass seals made by cult magic. This includes the binding sigils that mark Cthulhu's Vault. A character with one of these Dark Gifts can't gain another. A character with one of these gifts who leaves Innsmouth can choose to lose the Dark Gift or keep it.

name: Emerald Enclave
description:
A ranger guards a caravan through monster-plagued wilds. Forest defenders dismantle a war camp polluting a vital river. A circle of druids enacts a rain ritual for a drought-stricken village. These are but a few examples of how the Emerald Enclave makes the world a peaceful, hospitable place for people and nature alike.

The Emerald Enclave is an organization of survivalists and nature worshipers who refer to themselves as Caretakers. Members of the enclave maintain the balance between wilderness and civilization and reinforce what they call "the natural order." This natural order is exemplified by places where people and nature live in harmony—places where neither settlements nor wilds threaten to overwhelm the other. Caretakers protect such areas with their lives. To the Emerald Enclave, individual sacrifice is worthwhile if it means the preservation of the whole.

Caretakers wear green clothes made from natural, foraged materials such as plants and animal hides. The most powerful members have magically bright-green eyes. Most Caretakers are constantly surrounded by animals and can walk seamlessly between civilization and the wilds.

Members of the Emerald Enclave are loosely organized into diffuse subfactions called circles. Some Caretakers from the same circle might work together in small bands, but many operate in isolation. These lone wolves rely on the animals and plants around them to monitor other Caretakers (and non-Caretakers) in their vicinity.

# Goals and Activities

Caretakers preserve sacred natural sites by guarding them from logging, mining, and other exploitation. In areas where the natural order has already been compromised, the enclave restores the land so it is once again fruitful and hospitable. The enclave's spellcasters draw on nature magic to expedite labors such as planting trees and cleaning litter-filled waterways.

In dire situations—such as an undead-riddled battlefield—the Emerald Enclave leads coordinated assaults to root out the land's defilers. When necessary, Caretakers put impenitent evildoers to the sword. Members of the enclave don't relish violence against nature's children, but they know destruction is sometimes necessary for healing to begin. Caretakers do, however, proudly raise arms against unnatural forces such as aberrant monsters, reanimated dead, and machines of war. Members of the enclave believe such creatures exist to threaten the natural order and must be destroyed.

When they aren't healing broken lands or fending off the forces of chaos, Caretakers study and promote the ways that fauna and flora peacefully coexist in nature. Some spend time in settlements to forge new connections and encourage communities to tend the world around them. The enclave is always in search of allies, for, as one Caretaker saying puts it, the herd is strongest when its numbers are great. Thus, wise Caretakers hone their communication skills, knowing that a compelling speech or poignant adage can help others connect to the land.

**Lunar Rituals**  
The cycle of the moon and seasons is important to the Emerald Enclave's rituals. New Caretakers are initiated to the enclave each month on the full moon. New moons are reserved for tribunals, when judgment is passed on enemies taken prisoner or on Caretakers who've failed to uphold their duties. Many Caretakers plan sojourns to coincide with the lunar cycle so that they venture away from home while the moon wanes, then return while it waxes.

Just as the enclave shares in times of bounty, so too it shares the onus of performing necessary evils. When a tribunal demands capital punishment or a lunar ritual requires animal sacrifice, the tribunal selects an executioner through a casting of holy stones or sacred sticks or the summoning of a nature spirit that temporarily possesses an individual. In this way, no single Caretaker must bear the entire weight of the grisly work that must be done.

# Leadership and Organization

A Caretaker who achieves acclaim might take an epithet. Typically such an epithet is bestowed by another Caretaker to commemorate a worthy deed. Storied Caretakers have multiple epithets, which are then appended to one another; for example, a veteran enclave member named Krodar might be referred to as "Caretaker Krodar, Axe Breaker, and Tamer of Owlbears."

## Enclave Circles

A circle of the Emerald Enclave is a collective of Caretakers who study and practice the teachings of a particular aspect of the natural world to achieve the enclave's goals. Circles act independently, but they might seek one another's expertise when dealing with large-scale or far-ranging challenges.

There is some overlap between enclave circles and druid circles. But not all druids belong to the Emerald Enclave, and not all enclave members are druids. A druid of the Circle of the Moon, for example, might go their entire life without encountering the Emerald Enclave's circle of the same name, even though both groups practice similar teachings and rituals.

Each circle is led by its longest-serving and most accomplished members: sage rangers and ancient druids known as Verdant Ones. Verdant Ones lead lunar rituals, train new Caretakers, and coordinate missions with other circles. Often, a Verdant One passes judgment on issues where the balance between natural forces is unclear.

These are just a few of the enclave's circles in Faerûn:

**The Circle of Air** believes the world's eons-long natural cycle requires similarly lengthy study to fully comprehend.

**The Circle of the Ancients** is the oldest and most influential circle, tapping into primordial secrets.

**The Circle of the Giants** reveres the titans of the natural world: dinosaurs, dragons, and megafauna.

**The Circle of the Land** is the largest circle, protecting nature in all its forms and helping others survive in the wilderness.

**The Circle of the Moon** aids those who travel at night, and those threatened by nocturnal forces.

**The Circle of Wildfire** understands destruction is a fundamental part of the natural cycle and individual sacrifice is necessary for the greater good.

## The Three

The leaders of the Emerald Enclave are called the Three. These legendary druids provide guidance to other enclave circles and pass judgment on the most serious offenses. They occupy and protect a sacred temple to Silvanus called Oakenhall. Rarely the Three might visit another sacred site; such visits are never announced and rarely portend good news.

Though rarely spoken of as individuals, the Three are sometimes identified by the leaf-shaped masks they wear: the Oak, the Elm, and the Willow. The Three began as ordinary people, but when an individual dons one of these three magical masks, the mask merges with their flesh and transforms the wearer into a faceless, ageless being of no known species—nine feet tall and identical to the other members.

## Sacred Sites

All over Faerûn, Caretakers congregate at meeting grounds called sacred sites. Except for Oakenhall and a few other notable temples, the Emerald Enclave's sacred sites are naturally occurring locales of spiritual or magical import. The Emerald Enclave considers these sites—and any other locations where nature has worked its miracles—symbolically important and worth guarding closely. The following are a few notable sacred sites.

**Coltree.** In the foothills around the Spine of the World grows a massive fir called Coltree. It rises from a white granite slope ribboned with thick veins of exposed coal that give the landscape a zebra-like appearance.

**Moraeire.** Moraeire is a blue-tinted stone column in a valley of similar pillars off the west coast of the Sea of Fallen Stars. The valley is flooded most of the year, creating a unique ecosystem that's part bog, part canyon.

**Silver Tear.** The Silver Tear in Anauroch is an underground oasis at the center of a massive grotto. Its exact location is secret, but the entrance lies somewhere at the bottom of a steep gorge riddled with red caves.

# Renown Rewards

Characters gain renown with the Emerald Enclave by defending nature against would-be despoilers and by completing tasks for enclave members. As their Renown Score increases, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Emerald Enclave Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, your DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

**Emerald Enclave Renown**

| Renown Score | Reward |
|---|---|
| 3+ | You can hire Emerald Enclave hirelings for half the usual cost. |
| 5+ | You can request a Caretaker (Scout) to accompany you on a journey and help you navigate, forage, and search. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 10 | The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, a Caretaker teaches you Druidic. |
| 15+ | You can buy Common and Uncommon potions and Spell Scrolls from the Emerald Enclave. |
| 25+ | If you or your companions are at risk of suffering from dehydration or malnutrition while within 10 miles of an enclave site, Caretakers bring you enough food and water to meet your needs. |
| 30 | The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, Caretakers provide you with 1d4 Potions of Healing (superior). |
| 40+ | Your eyes turn bright green. Centaurs, treants, unicorns, and all Beasts are Friendly to you by default. |
| 50+ | Members of the Emerald Enclave openly share information with you. In addition, you can request a single audience with the Three. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again. |

# Emerald Enclave Characters

Adventurers who commit their lives to the Emerald Enclave are often Barbarians, Druids, or Rangers, but anyone who honors and protects the natural balance can find a place in the enclave. Those who spent their formative years around the Emerald Enclave might have the Guide or Hermit background.

**Member Benefits**  
If you're a member of the Emerald Enclave, you receive these benefits.

**Modest Lifestyle.** The Emerald Enclave provides its members with enough food, water, and shelter for a Modest lifestyle.

**Trinket.** Roll on the Emerald Enclave Trinkets table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Emerald Enclave.

**Emerald Enclave Trinkets**

| 1d6 | Trinket |
|---|---|
| 1 | A pair of earrings made from oak leaves that never wilt |
| 2 | A miniature model cottage made of twigs |
| 3 | A green-glowing firefly in a bottle |
| 4 | A gourd that sounds like rustling leaves when held to one's ear |
| 5 | A preserved rabbit's foot on a leather strap |
| 6 | An antler shaped like an Elvish rune |

# Special Facility

Members of the Emerald Enclave can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

**Emerald Enclave Grove**  
*Level 9 Bastion Facility*

**Prerequisite:** Membership in the Emerald Enclave

**Space:** Vast

**Hirelings:** 2

**Order:** Recruit

Veteran agents of the Emerald Enclave create safe havens with trees, grass, and flowing water, where magical creatures that embody the power of nature live in peace and safety. The Emerald Enclave Grove can house one Huge creature or two Large creatures; four Small or Medium creatures or eight Tiny creatures can occupy the same space as one Large creature there.

**Recruit: Creature of Nature.** When you issue the Recruit order to this facility, you invite a creature from the Emerald Enclave Grove Creatures table to your Emerald Enclave Grove. Roll any die. If the number rolled is odd, the creature doesn't accept your invitation and you gain no benefit from having issued the order. If the number rolled is even, a creature accepts your invitation and moves into your Emerald Enclave Grove after 7 days. Your hirelings care for the creature and perform upkeep in the facility.

Creatures in your Emerald Enclave Grove count as Bastion Defenders. Deduct any you lose from your Bastion Defenders roster. You can choose not to count one or more of these creatures as Bastion Defenders, in which case they can't be called on to defend the Bastion. Instead, they act in accordance with their nature and use their stat blocks in the Monster Manual.

**Emerald Enclave Grove Creatures**

| Creature | Size |
|---|---|
| Awakened Shrub | Small |
| Awakened Tree | Huge |
| Blink Dog | Medium |
| Centaur Trooper | Large |
| Dryad | Medium |
| Myconid Adult | Medium |
| Myconid Sprout | Small |
| Pixie | Tiny |
| Satyr | Medium |
| Sprite | Tiny |
| Treant | Large |
| Unicorn | Large |

name: Factions and Renown
description:
Renown is an optional rule you can use to track characters' standing, individually or as a party, within a particular group, such as a faction, an organization, or a community.

A character's or party's Renown Score starts at 0, then increases as characters earn favor and reputation with respect to the group. You can tie benefits to a character's renown, including ranks, titles, and access to resources.

Players track renown separately for each group their characters are associated with. For example, an adventurer might have a Renown Score of 5 with one faction and a Renown Score of 20 with another, based on the character's interaction with each group.

You can use renown over the course of an entire campaign or within a single adventure. At a campaign scale, you might set up factions or guilds that characters can join, individually or as a group, and the characters pursue ranks and rewards by gaining Renown within their organizations. At an adventure level, you might decide that the characters as a group need to earn a Renown Score of 5+ with the council before the council trusts the characters enough to share resources with them.

# Gaining Renown

At your discretion, a character or party can increase their renown in the following ways:

**Completing Missions.** Advancing a group's interests increases a character's Renown Score within that group by 1. Completing a mission specifically assigned by that group or that directly benefits the group increases the character's Renown Score by 2. Hugely significant quests might grant Renown Score increases of 3 or 4 at once.

**Group Involvement.** Once a character has established a Renown Score of 1+ with a group, the character can gain renown by spending time between adventures undertaking minor tasks for the group and socializing with its members. After doing so for a number of days equal to 10 times the character's current Renown Score, the character's Renown Score increases by 1.

# Benefits of Renown

Use these guidelines when determining the benefits of increasing renown.

**Recognition**  
A character who has a Renown Score of 3+ with a group is a respected member of that group. Other members of the group are Friendly toward the character by default and provide the character with lodging and food in dire circumstances.

**Rank**  
Some groups have hierarchies that characters can ascend as they improve their Renown Scores. Other groups have positions of honor that characters can apply for if their Renown Score is high enough. Characters can earn promotions as their Renown Scores increase. You can establish certain Renown Score thresholds as prerequisites (though not necessarily the only prerequisites) for advancing in rank. You can set these thresholds however you like, creating ranks and titles for the groups in your campaign.

**Perks**  
Earning renown within a group might come with certain benefits. A character with a Renown Score of 3+ might gain access to a reliable contact, a safe house, or a discount on adventuring gear. With a Renown Score of 10+, a character might gain access to Potions and Scrolls, the ability to call in a favor, or backup on dangerous missions. A character whose Renown Score rises to 50 might be able to call on a small army, acquire a Rare magic item, gain access to a helpful spellcaster, or assign special missions to members of lower status.

# Losing Renown

Disagreements with members of a group aren't enough to cause a loss of renown within that group. However, serious offenses committed against the group or its members can result in a loss of renown and rank within the organization. The extent of the loss depends on the infraction and is left to your discretion. A character's Renown Score with a group can never drop below 0.

# Level-Based Renown

If you want to use the benefits of renown without tracking Renown Scores, you can use a character's level as a shorthand for the character's Renown Score with a group, assuming the character has worked with or for that group for most of the character's career. The Level-Based Renown table shows equivalencies between Renown Score and character level.

| Renown Score | Character Level |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1 |
| 3 | 3 |
| 10 | 5 |
| 25 | 11 |
| 50 | 17 |
